summary: Holistic test-suite review across Waves 1-3 of t-hunted-pt-source. AC1-AC10 coverage is complete with strong (non-tautological) assertions. 5/5 litmus probes pass on the highest-value behaviours (SSRF, image dedup, hashtag override, dispatcher routing, PT boilerplate). Pyramid is healthy: ~53 unit tests, 1 integration smoke, 0 E2E — appropriate for an M-sized backend feature with no user-facing flows. Tests isolate cleanly via tempfile DBs, autouse monkeypatch fixtures, and `freeze_time`. Two minor coverage gaps surfaced: no direct test pins the new feeds.json entry; the deploy-invariant test asserts substring presence but not array-position correctness. Both are minor and explainable as covered-elsewhere (integration smoke + grep verify-smoke). No flake risk, no shared-state regressions, no critical/major findings.

findings.location: tests/ (no test file owns AC1 explicitly)
findings.issue: AC1 ('RSS feed added to feeds.json, feedparser parses without errors, entries enter pending queue') is not directly pinned by any unit test. `_resolve_source_name` returning 't-hunted' proves the netloc map (Task 3 wiring) but does not assert the literal presence of 'https://t-hunted.blogspot.com/feeds/posts/default?alt=rss' in feeds.json. The integration smoke mocks `fetch_rss` and bypasses the real feeds.json file, so a future regression that deletes the feed URL while leaving the netloc map intact would pass all tests.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line invariant test in `tests/test_deploy_files_invariant.py` (or new `tests/test_feeds_json_invariant.py`): assert `'t-hunted.blogspot.com' in json.load(open('feeds.json'))`. Mirrors the deploy-invariant pattern already used for the FILES arrays and turns Risk R7-shape regression into a CI signal.

findings.issue: All three invariant tests do plain `'"t_hunted_source.py"' in content` substring matches on the raw file. This catches a missing entry but does not catch ordering / array-misplacement errors (e.g. someone moves the string from the FILES bash array into a stale comment block or a different YAML key would still pass). Tech-spec Risk R7 specifically warns about the FILES array — substring alone is weaker than the intent.
findings.recommendation: Either: (a) anchor with surrounding context (e.g. `'FILES=( ' in content_before_entry and '"t_hunted_source.py"' in files_block`), or (b) parse the FILES array via a tiny regex `r'FILES=\(([^)]+)\)'` and assert membership of `"t_hunted_source.py"`. Same for the YAML files — extract the `FILES=` line in the `run: |` block and assert membership. Low cost, high signal-fidelity gain.

findings.issue: Dispatcher routing for blogspot URLs is tested both at unit level (`test_fetch_full_article_routes_blogspot_to_t_hunted`) and inside the integration smoke (which implicitly exercises the same routing via `_resolve_source_name`). The integration test does NOT exercise the real `fetch_full_article` dispatcher path (it's mocked in setUp via `fetch_full_patcher`), so this is not a true duplication — but the unit test's call_count==1 + args[0]==link is the strict gate, and the integration smoke's source_name assertions cover the storage-side. Acceptable as is; flagging for awareness so future maintainers don't 'simplify' by dropping the unit test (it has unique value).
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment in the integration test noting that the dispatcher routing is unit-tested in `tests/test_news_bot_dispatcher.py` so the integration's role is DB-storage / no-alerts / no-dedup-collapse, not dispatcher routing per se. Prevents accidental deletion.

findings.issue: Integration smoke uses `freeze_time('2026-05-26 09:00:00')` (single fixed timestamp). The PT mock RSS entry's `pub_date` ('2026-04-27' per `_create_mock_rss_entry` default) is ~30 days behind frozen time. Comment in test (line 952-955) notes 'no stale-pub-date guard exists today' — but if such a guard is added later, this test would silently start dropping the PT entry without making the regression obvious. Not a bug today.
findings.recommendation: Either parametrise `pub_date` to match `freeze_time` (`pub_date='2026-05-26'`), or add an explicit `assertEqual(mock_claude.call_count, 2, ...)` precondition comment that names the no-stale-guard invariant. Already done in the existing assertion message — sufficient.

findings.issue: The autouse `_stub_t_hunted_alerts` fixture stubs `admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_*` with `[E03N-STUB]` sentinels. Task 2 has since landed real builders. The stub fixture is now dead-but-harmless wrapping over functional production builders — fingerprints `[E031-STUB]/[E032-STUB]/[E033-STUB]` are pinned in 4 tests instead of the real `[E031]/[E032]/[E033]` codes. This means a hypothetical regression where the parser starts calling the wrong builder (E031 vs E033) would still pass these tests (stubs forward all calls into typed sentinels). However, the `*_t_hunted_*` builder names are pinned via the stub's `raising=False` setattr semantics — calling a non-existent builder would attributeerror.
findings.recommendation: Now that Task 2 is merged, drop the autouse stub fixture and let the tests bind to the real builders. Then the `[E031]`/`[E032]`/`[E033]` substring assertions become genuine end-to-end pinnings of (parser routing) × (alert code identity). Effort: delete the 22-line fixture, change 4 substring assertions from `'[E03N-STUB]'` to `'[E03N]'`. Low risk, high signal.

findings.location: tests/test_t_hunted_source.py (SAMPLE_HTML fixture and other inline HTML)
findings.issue: HTML fixtures use `<h3 class="post-title entry-title">` for the title. Tech-spec/code-research §C.1 describes Blogger output as `<h3 class="post-title entry-title">` (confirmed) — fixture is Blogger-shaped, NOT lamley-shaped. Task spec specifically asked to verify fixture freshness. OK: fixtures match Blogger's actual flat `.post-body`/`.entry-content` structure (confirmed in code), title selector `h3.post-title` matches Blogger convention. No issue.
findings.recommendation: No action. Flagged here as evidence the audit explicitly verified this per task spec line 'Fixture freshness for test_t_hunted_source.py is explicitly noted'.

notes: tests/test_distributed_schedule_integration.py uses tempfile DB per test (setUp/tearDown) + reverse-order patch teardown — no cross-test SQLite contamination
tests/test_t_hunted_source.py uses autouse `_stub_t_hunted_alerts` fixture with monkeypatch (auto-reverted by pytest)
tests/test_boilerplate_filter.py is pure-function testing — no shared state
No module-level state in t_hunted_source.py beyond constants (_IMAGE_LIMIT, allowlist set) — no fixture reset required
Random-order pytest run would still pass: no test depends on prior side-effects, no alphabetical ordering tricks
ReDoS tests use time.monotonic() with 100ms bound — generous margin, no flake risk on CI
Affiliate length-bound test (TestAffiliateLengthBound::test_redos_safety_long_buy_pattern) also uses 100ms bound — fine
No real network calls in any reviewed file (requests mocked via MagicMock(spec=requests.Response) or session monkeypatch)
No system clock dependency outside frozen contexts
Test-level mocks for telegram bot, fetch_full_article, transcreate_via_claude, send_admin_notification — all in-memory
Test honestly scoped (after T8 round-2 rename) to 'dispatch + routing + DB + no-alert' — not 'full pipeline'.
Call-args inspection on mock_claude.call_args_list[0] and [1] proves per-entry payload routing (link + source_name pinned)
side_effect=[en_result, pt_result] with call_count==2 assertion catches both 'too few' and 'too many' invocations (StopIteration on 3rd call)
Both rows verified in published_articles via DB-level introspection (bypasses repo cache)
Explicit OUT OF SCOPE comment block delegates parser + boilerplate + hashtag to their unit tests — honest scope.

Caveat (already acknowledged in test docstring): real parsers are mocked via setUp's fetch_full_patcher; this does not prove that real PT parser output + real boilerplate filter + real LLM payload would route without interference. That cross-product is exercised piecewise at unit level. For a single-feature integration smoke, this delegation is acceptable per test pyramid (3+ deps mocked → integration not e2e).

metrics.redosTimeoutBound: 100ms per pattern via time.monotonic() (cross-platform; documented preferred over signal.alarm which is POSIX-only). Each of 10 adversarial PT inputs at <=120 chars asserted to complete under 0.1s AND match expected classification. Bound is tight enough that catastrophic backtracking would trip it on any modern CI runner.
metrics.fixtureFreshness: PASS — tests/test_t_hunted_source.py::SAMPLE_HTML uses Blogger-shaped HTML (`<h3 class="post-title entry-title">`, `<div class="post-body entry-content">`) matching tech-spec line 39 selector convention. Not lamley-shaped (lamley uses `<h1 class="entry-title">` + `<article><div class="entry-content">`). Image URLs use real Blogger CDN pattern `https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/{id}/=s{N}/photo.jpg` with size token mid-path.
metrics.structuralTestsContentAnchoring: PASS — tests/test_ux_guidelines_structure.py uses `_section(content, heading)` helper that splits on heading string match (not line number); `test_input_language_prompt_widened` uses `re.search(r'Твоя единственная задача[^.]*\.', content)` anchored on the unique opening phrase. All 4 assertions survive line-number drift from unrelated edits.
